scope: Public-API isolation of the historical Slang CPU rigid-direct angular-velocity mismatch

frame_20.result: CPU and CUDA dynamic-box state is byte-for-value identical and both report zero rigid contacts

first_exact_difference.classification: below unchanged tolerance and reconverged exactly by frame 20

first_contract_failure.trigger: first submission after the frame-20 kinematic target move
first_contract_failure.contacts: both drivers report eight dynamic-box/kinematic-box contacts, but their impulse records cannot be paired within the direct tolerance

historical_golden_classification.cpu_result: failed exactly the three documented frame-40 dynamic-box angular-velocity components; maximum absolute error 0.0002557467669248581
historical_golden_classification.same_revision_gtx1080_cuda_result: also failed historical RTX 3050 Ti reference regression for frame-40 combined_momentum[2] and angular_velocity[1]
historical_golden_classification.conclusion: The original report combined a real CPU/CUDA first-contact divergence with smaller historical-device/reference drift; it was not a pure final-integration error.

current_main_capture.same_revision_result: PASS: all 61 frames compare within the unchanged direct tolerance
current_main_capture.first_exact_difference: frame 21 dynamic-box.position[1], one float ULP (1.1920928955078125e-7), within tolerance
current_main_capture.historical_golden_result: Both current CPU and CUDA fail the same 13 frame-40 fields against the retained golden, so remaining drift is shared rather than CPU-specific.

reproduction: Build revision 603fee51dfc67b095f86641724f46752046b56fa once with PARALLEL_MATER_BUILD_SLANG_CPU_DRIVER=ON and once with PARALLEL_MATER_BUILD_CUDA=ON, PARALLEL_MATER_BUILD_CONFORMANCE=ON, Slang 2026.18, Release and all unrelated drivers/gallery disabled.
Set PM_DRIVER_FILES and PM_LAYER_FILES to each build's generated driver and validation manifests, then run: parallel-mater-conformance --case rigid-direct --every-frame --output <backend-output>.
python3 conformance/v1/compare.py --cases conformance/v1/cases --expected <cuda-output> --actual <cpu-output> --case rigid-direct --report <report>; expected result is failure beginning at frame 21.
Repeat the two runner commands from revision 3acb4130ef939497d9b36d4f14c1c280f99892a3; the same comparator command passes all 61 frames.

corrective_follow_up.title: Adjudicate rigid-direct reference drift
corrective_follow_up.reason: Current CPU/CUDA agreement removes the old CPU-only classification, but agreement cannot decide whether the shared frame-21 response or the retained historical reference is physically correct.

limitations: This evidence isolates public observable state and contact outputs; it does not identify a private kernel instruction or establish an independent physical oracle.
The historical reference came from an RTX 3050 Ti and commit cc2a2e4; the same-revision CUDA reproduction uses this GTX 1080 and commit 603fee5.
Cross-driver agreement and reference regression are not physical-quality qualification. F5-17 keeps the unresolved reference adjudication visible without changing tolerances or goldens.
